supercharger_access.notes: Quick web lookup. Canadian article (Sept 2024) on the GM NACS adapter for Canadian owners of Blazer EV, Equinox EV, Silverado EV and LYRIQ. Says nothing about 2026 trim ports.

US page: CCS1 cars use Superchargers with the GM-approved NACS adapter ($299) / optional adapter in GM's spec guide. Current state for model year 2026: adapter needed. Markets: CA/US. (2026 car: same port and adapter state as the 2025 car on this model.)

charge_port.notes: Estimated: CCS1 (J1772 native inlet) through the 2026 model year: press pages for this model line state CCS1 for 2024-2026 and NACS from 2027. Same port assumed for the Canadian car (Guide Auto 2024-09-18: Canadian owners need the GM adapter). Model year 2026. (2026 car: same port and adapter state as the 2025 car on this model.)

consumption_highway_wh_per_km.notes: Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, upper 60s to ~80 F (about 20-27 C), wheel size not stated, battery-side (vehicle energy gauge) | 2023 Lyriq RWD (same generation; Cadillac-listed usable 102 kWh). 104.7 kWh over 330 mi: 104.7 / 330 = 317.3 Wh/mi / 1.609344 = 197 Wh/km (article says 3.1 mi/kWh). Other test seen: Car and Driver 75 mph, 2023 RWD 20-inch, 270 mi (via Autoblog, no consumption). | Main session: the page calls 102 kWh usable while our data has 95 usable / 100.4 gross, and the gauge read 104.7 kWh used; 2023 to 2026 RWD pack/motor match is plausible but not confirmed.

wheels.notes: US Cars.com: Luxury RWD 20 in aluminum, 265/50R20. CarGurus: 20 in standard on non-Signature trims. Signature trims are 22 in standard, so this is the base size.
CarGurus: 22 in available on Luxury, Sport, Premium Luxury, Premium Sport (standard on Signature).
